chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad ibn Usman, from Ubaydullah ibn Ali al-Halbi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Any man who commits fornication with a woman, then it becomes pleasing to him to marry her, [the ruling is] permissible. He said: Its beginning is fornication (zina), and its end is marriage. And its example is like that of a palm tree: a man takes its fruit unlawfully, then he buys it afterwards, so it becomes permissible for him.
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on a man who marries a woman after committing fornication with her?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that marrying a woman after committing fornication with her is valid, using the analogy of unlawfully taking fruit from a palm tree and then purchasing the tree to legitimize ownership. This hadith, found in *Al-Kafi*, addresses the juristic question of whether the initial illicit act invalidates the subsequent marriage contract, affirming its permissibility despite the prior sin. The analogy highlights the distinction between the act itself and the legal status of the relationship, a key concept in Shia fiqh regarding the validity of nikah after zina.
